hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline to find the normal reaction: $R = mg\cos\theta$.
Calculate the friction force $F = \mu R$ opposing the motion up the plane.
Because the particle moves at constant speed, the pulling force $T$ balances friction plus the component of weight down the plane: $T = F + mg\sin\theta$.
Calculate the work done by the force using $W = T \times d$ with $d = 2.5\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
From $\tan\theta = \frac{5}{12}$, construct a right-angled triangle with opposite side $5$ and adjacent side $12$. The hypotenuse is $\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}, \quad \cos\theta = \frac{12}{13}$$

Calculate the normal reaction force $R$ perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$R = mg\cos\theta$$
Substitute $m = 13\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\cos\theta = \frac{12}{13}$:
$$R = 13 \times 10 \times \frac{12}{13} = 130 \times \frac{12}{13} = 120\text{ N}$$

State the friction formula for motion along a rough surface:
$$F = \mu R$$
Substitute $\mu = 0.3$ and $R = 120\text{ N}$:
$$F = 0.3 \times 120 = 36\text{ N}$$
Because the particle moves up the slope, friction acts downwards along the slope.

Write the equation of motion along the plane. Since the particle moves at constant speed, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$):
$$T - F - mg\sin\theta = 0$$
$$T = F + mg\sin\theta$$
Substitute $F = 36\text{ N}$ and the component of weight $mg\sin\theta = 13 \times 10 \times \frac{5}{13} = 50\text{ N}$:
$$T = 36 + 50 = 86\text{ N}$$

State the formula for work done by a constant force along the displacement:
$$W = T \times d$$
Substitute $T = 86\text{ N}$ and displacement $d = 2.5\text{ m}$:
$$W = 86 \times 2.5 = 215\text{ J}$$
Thus the work done by the force is $215\text{ J}$.
